correctness.rationale: Concavity and symmetry reduce all weights without losing unrestricted optimality. The rim Fourier eigenvalues and 3-dimensional quotient eigenvalue quadratic were reconstructed. The normalized gap constraint has the exact feasible section c>=f_m(a) for a>2/(m+2), with least rim weight max(0,(1-a)/delta_m). The strictly convex scalar cost has a unique minimizer: interior for m=3,4,5 and boundary a=1 for m>=6. Averaging of arbitrary optima and nonnegativity give zero every rim edge at m>=6. Exact symbolic derivative and closed-form cost identities checked; 468 finite numerical comparisons independently assembled but do not constitute infinite proof.

value.rationale: For a canonical ring-with-hub network and a physically motivated spare hub leaf, the theorem gives explicit globally optimal conductances and a sharp support-screening transition at six rim vertices, including a rigidity statement for every asymmetric optimum. A generic SDP does not itself communicate this closed-form design law; the exact cutoff is a meaningful natural structural invariant.
